neighbours.label: Public-health guidance language: agencies or experts recommending, advising against, or setting health-based limits for a practice ('no longer recommends daily aspirin', 'health-based limit', 'standard of care'), vs the same sentence frames about non-health matters
fire: The panel no longer recommends routine vitamin D screening for healthy adults.
Federal regulators set a health-based limit for arsenic in rice products.
The college advises against antibiotics for most sore throats in children.
Experts now recommend that pregnant women limit tuna to one serving a week.
The new guideline recommends blood pressure checks every year after forty.
The agency lowered the safe exposure level for lead in children's toys.
Health officials recommend against screening low-risk women under forty.
The society's statement was not meant to serve as a standard of care for surgeons.
quiet: The library no longer opens routine study rooms for evening groups.
Federal regulators set a price limit for imported rice products.
The college advises against parking on the main road during exams.
Experts now recommend that hikers carry a map on long trails.
The new timetable runs trains every hour after nine.
The agency lowered the speed limit near the children's park.
Travel officials recommend against driving through the pass at night.
The society's statement was not meant to serve as a rulebook for chess clubs.

predictions: Health-guidance items reach 0.25-0.5; non-health twins stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: peaks on ' to', '-based', ' longer', ' would' in health advisories (EPA, Task Force, 'no longer recommends daily aspirin'); the logit effect promotes ' recommendation', ' risk', ' recommended'. Probe: 'Task Force no longer recommends daily aspirin' 0.468, 'health-based limit' 0.400, 'not designed to serve as a standard of care' 0.331, 'whether ... identify low-risk patients' 0.219; non-health twins 'museum no longer opens' 0.112, 'buy that car' 0.116, 'bridge not designed' 0.042.
